chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibn Bukayr from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurara ibn A'yan who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman in Iraq, then traveled to Syria and married another woman, who turned out to be the sister of the woman in Iraq. He said: He is separated from the one he married in Syria, and he does not approach her until the waiting period of the Syrian woman expires. I said: If he marries a woman, then marries her mother, while he does not know that she is her mother? He said: God the Exalted has excused his ignorance in that. Then he said: When he knows that she is her mother, he should not approach her, nor approach the daughter, until the waiting period of the mother expires from him. When the mother's waiting period expires, it becomes lawful for him to marry the daughter. I said: If the mother bears a child? He said: It is his child, and it will be his son and the brother of his wife.

key_terms.الشَّامِيَّةِ: The Syrian woman (referring to the wife in Syria)
key_terms.عِدَّةُ: Waiting period (iddah) after marriage or divorce

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for a man who unknowingly marries a mother and daughter or two sisters?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Isfahani's chain within al-Istibsar, this hadith clarifies the fiqh of 'Ikhtilat' (mixing of marriages) by distinguishing between marrying two sisters versus a mother and daughter. It establishes that while ignorance exempts the man from penalty, he must separate from the second wife and await her 'iddah before consummating that specific union, ensuring lineage clarity for any offspring born during the interim.
